introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 2 (0730), June 2019, ADVANCED LEVEL. Paper 2: Section A - Summary and Text Reconstruction; Section B - Composition; Section C - Prescribed Texts. Duration: THREE HOURS.**

Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Begin with SECTION A.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure considered as an attempt to cheat will earn you a penalty.

In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you no marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

A pre-prepared or memorized composition will earn you no marks.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (20 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (06 marks); Expression (08 marks); Accuracy (06 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write about from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 500 and 550 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **e)** Describe an incident in your school which led to the dismissal of many students and say how this incident has affected your life.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: the incident and its consequence (31 dismissals).
2. Causes: the new rules and the rumour of a protest.
3. The escalation and the narrator's role as a silent witness.
4. The dismissals and the friend's departure.
5. Effects on the narrator's life and conclusion.

**Model composition (517 words)**

It was the third week of the first term, in my Upper Sixth year, when an incident occurred at our school that I shall remember for the rest of my life. It led to the dismissal of thirty-one students, among them my closest friend, Ndifor, and it changed my understanding of discipline, friendship and responsibility.

The trouble began over the school's new rules. Our principal had banned mobile phones, introduced compulsory evening study and announced that students who arrived late would pay a fine. Many boys considered these measures unjust, and on Monday morning a rumour spread that a "peaceful protest" would be held after the break. I did not take it seriously. During the break, however, a group of senior students gathered near the football field, shouting slogans and beating on empty buckets. Within minutes the crowd had grown, and others, caught up in the excitement, joined without knowing what they were protesting about.

Things worsened quickly. Anger replaced reason, and the crowd, which a minute earlier had been merely noisy, became dangerous. Someone threw a stone, and a window of the administration block broke with a loud crash. A few students pushed over the principal's flower pots and tore down the notice board. When the vice principal tried to calm them, he was jostled and insulted. Teachers ran across the compound, the bell rang continuously, and the gendarmes were called. By evening, the compound resembled a battlefield. I stood at the edge of the crowd, afraid and silent, because I had the courage neither to leave nor to speak.

The next day, the disciplinary council met. Every student who had been identified in the photographs taken by teachers was summoned, and thirty-one were dismissed for good. Ndifor, who had only followed the crowd and had thrown nothing, was among them. I watched him pack his trunk in silence, while his father, a poor farmer who had sold his goats to pay the fees, waited at the gate with bowed head. I could say nothing to console either of them.

That event affected my life in several ways. First, it taught me the cost of acting without thinking. Ndifor's future was damaged in a moment, because he allowed the noise of the crowd to replace his own judgement. Second, it taught me that legitimate complaints should be presented through proper channels, such as the student council and the parents' association, and not through violence. Third, I resolved to use my voice. When I was elected school prefect in the second term, I persuaded the administration to meet the students every month, and the school was never disturbed again. Finally, it taught me the value of loyalty: I visited Ndifor during every holiday and helped him to prepare for the examination as a private candidate, and he eventually passed.

Today, whenever I am tempted to follow the crowd, I recall that sad evening and the silence of a father waiting at a gate. The lesson I learnt has become the compass of my life: freedom is worthless without responsibility, and a wise person thinks before he acts.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 6 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 8 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 6 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Describing an incident that did not lead to the dismissal of students, or forgetting to say how it affected the writer's life.
2. Revealing a real name or school (the rubric forbids disclosing one's identity) and a story with no organisation.

incertitudes: Consigne de la page de garde (règle de choix) : « Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet ». Section A obligatoire (aucune règle), Section B : 1 sujet sur 6 (a à f), Section C : 1 question sur 4. Les regles_choix sont identiques dans les 12 fichiers.

Fautes imprimées dans le sujet, laissées telles quelles : titre « SECTION A SUMMERY AND TEXT RECONSTRUCTION » (summary), « for few hours » (Q1), « A this stage », « into the will » (mill), « The stripped cane are then », « out of them » (Q2, forme reconstruite) ; Section C question 2 : « Use any Three prescribed text ».
Le tiret cadratin du passage de résumé (« choice of home - among the stinging tentacles ») est écrit « - » conformément à la règle du projet. Le passage ne porte pas de numéros de ligne imprimés.

Section A : le sujet imprime 30 marks pour la section (15 par question). La répartition des 15 points du résumé n'est pas imprimée : la grille du corrigé est indicative. La reconstruction est comptée à 1 point par blanc (15 blancs), ce qui est une hypothèse ; plusieurs réponses sont acceptables pour certains blancs (voir le corrigé).

Section B : 20 marks (Content and Organisation 6, Expression 8, Accuracy 6), 500 à 550 mots demandés. Points imprimés non corrigés. Compositions modèles : comptes de mots faits par script (de 517 à 534 mots).
